content.title: The Drama (2026) ⭐ 7.5 | Comedy, Drama, Romance
content.text: Videos8Featured reviewsGreat black comedyThe Drama is very comfortable being an uncomfortable viewing experience. It starts off in a cute and cosy fashion before revealing a dark secret that definitely gets a reaction and unlocks an equally dark sense of humour in everything afterwards. It's hard to watch this seemingly idyllic wedding falling apart but at the same time it's impossible to look away and the film generally is a great exploration of how messy people can be because of how hard it is to understand who a person really is.Robert Pattinson and Zendaya are amazing together thanks to their natural chemistry and the uncomfortableness that gradually builds between them is just as strong. It's especially hard to look away when watching Robert Pattinson's character really fall apart by continuing to make bad decisions which only make things worse as he truly unravels after hearing the big reveal wisely kept out of the trailers. There's also a couple of strong turns from Alana Haim and Mamoudou Athie.Writer & director Kristoffer Borgli always has a firm grasp on the film's tone and delivers a black comedy that's designed to spark many conversations about the morally murky nature of its most shocking reveals as well as how the characters react to it. The deliberately abrupt and effectively nonlinear editing by Kristoffer Borgli and Joshua Raymond Lee brings you up to speed on how this sweet relationship came to be really quickly and enhances the comedy with its sharp timing.Not perfect, but memorably intense and very well-acted.The more unbearable The Drama got, the better. There's an extreme amount of anxiety here, especially in the second half, that I was there for. That's my thing. That's what I like. That's what I find funny (see anything Safdie-related, and Lanthimos at his best, too, if you want modern directors who are doing that kind of thing well). Add Kristoffer Borgli to the list, maybe.This was a little better than his last movie, Dream Scenario, which I also liked quite a lot, so I'll have to check out Sick of Myself. Dream Scenario was like a psychological comedy, and The Drama is like a rom-com colliding at high speed into a psychological drama/thriller/borderline-horror movie. It takes a little while to find its footing, but then it builds well once it does.It peaks in the final act, but I imagine it would've been difficult to end a movie like this. Borgoli doesn't really stick the landing, but at least the ending doesn't ruin the movie. You're just waving this high-intensity wave, and it doesn't come crashing down quite like how it should, at the end. Almost, but not quite.Still, it's a good ride until then. If anyone has seen Sleeping Dogs Lie (not really recommended, but it is brave), then this is like a slightly less gutsy but also more entertaining spin on that kind of story; a relationship between two soon-to-be-married people being tested when a difficult thing about one person's past is revealed. Zendaya is great in the first half, and then Pattinson largely dominates the second half. Both are great. Alana Haim is also really good here, in a supporting role.It's also great to see Pattinson rebound after two movies in 2025 that were misses, in my eyes (the frankly kind of awful Mickey 17 and the ambitious but super flawed/frustrating Die My Love... Die My Love also had some real relationship drama and a messy wedding, so maybe it would be a good double feature with The Drama if you like Robert Pattinson and are also a sicko).One of the most bizarre films I've seen in theatres"The Drama" doesn't feel like a real movie, and even after just getting out of the theatre, I'm still not convinced it is. As I was watching it, I almost started to convince myself that I was about to wake up at any moment - the movie feels like something I dreamt up after a night of heavy drinking; just surreal. I watched this in a virtually empty auditorium, which is a shame because I really wish I knew how the average audience would react to this - crowd pleasing this is not.Advertised as a romantic comedy, "The Drama" deals with surprisingly heavy, uncomfortable, and quite honestly, shocking content. In today's day and age especially, I was a bit taken aback at what exactly the movie was about. Nothing inherently disturbing happens in the film, but the subject matter itself is indeed disturbing, and I'm surprised that this idea was greenlit, filmed, and widely released - on Easter Weekend, no less! But now that all of that is out of the way, how is the movie?Your reaction to the subject matter is going to deeply dictate your opinion on this film. My mother, for example, found it "painful" to watch; while I didn't find this movie painful, I did find it uncomfortable but entertaining. As a fan of both Zendaya and Robert Pattinson, I found a lot to enjoy here - there is a charm to their relationship, and I enjoyed watching how a simple, ordinary, but happy relationship developed. I also found it interesting to watch how a simple, ordinary, and happy relationship can potentially start to deteriorate when you find out something unexpected about your partner. Pattinson and Zendaya have really good chemistry, and it was fun to see their different reactions to the situations they found themselves in - from panic and anxiety to anger and distrust, both actors go through many emotional stages, and it was fascinating to witness.The movie also had a very unique editing style that I think contributed to its dreamy feeling. Images and sounds would sometimes pop in or out, just like they would in a dream or as you're drifting off to sleep; it was a unique, unexpected decision that made the movie interesting to watch. That said, the movie also felt kind of uneventful in a way that's sort of hard to explain. A lot does happen in this movie in terms of just the wide range of emotions that people experience, but when it comes to things actually happening, not much happens - I hope this makes sense.I don't know. I just feel weird about this movie. I liked watching it well-enough, but the subject matter is so bizarre that I'm still in shock that this movie even exists. I'm glad I watched it, and I was entertained while I was watching it, but I can't say I'd actively recommend "The Drama."If you have emetophobia, maybe stay away from this one.If you have emetophobia, maybe stay away from this one.It's a strange case, honestly. The idea is genuinely interesting-there's something unique at its core that makes it stick in your head longer than most dramas. It's not forgettable, I'll give it that. But at the same time, it never really lands.The performances are easily the best part. Zendaya and Pattinson carry the film with real presence and effort-you can feel they're giving it everything. Visually, it's also solid, with some genuinely beautiful cinematography that tries to elevate the material.But the real problem is the writing. The story feels oddly empty, like it's building toward something that never comes. Scene after scene just drifts by, and instead of emotional weight, you're left feeling... tired. There's no real payoff, no strong connection, nothing to truly hold onto.It's a simple drama dressed up as something deeper and more profound than it actually is. Unique? Yes. Memorable? In a way. But ultimately, it feels hollow-like a film that has all the pieces, yet somehow nothing to say.A24 Is Single-Handedly Keeping Cinema Alive in the Age of Superheroes and Sequels.Loved it. It was a great mix of edginess, craziness, and discomfort, mixed in with humorous moments, irony, and dark humor. Classic A24.I think Robert Pattinson could win an Oscar for his role. He was so good-especially at the end of the movie with the wedding speech scene, and then the scene when he gets home after that. Just unbelievable acting. Super impressive.Zendaya was great as well, and while her character didn't get as much spotlight as Pattinson's, she still really crushed her parts.All the characters are complex. None of them are necessarily right or wrong, good or bad. The film does a great job of showing the hypocrisy of some people's beliefs. Is it worse to do something bad on impulse? Or is it worse to back out of doing something seriously planned that is super heinous?It also asks: can people change over time? Just because somebody was a bad person or had skeletons in their closet a long time ago, does that make them a bad person now?It's also a really good exploration of how instability can start eating away at you once you begin questioning what you thought you knew. The directors did such a good job showing how every little action gets overthought because of new information. It begs the question: is ignorance bliss?The cinematography is fantastic, as always for A24. Costume and makeup were all on point. The setting was very cool-I wish I had the loft the main characters were living in. It's literally a young person's dream apartment.The editing was superb. It took a second to adjust to the jump cuts and flashbacks, but once you got the hang of the pacing, it really added to the experience and the uneasiness of the whole atmosphere.10/10.
